After clear_selection, nothing is selected: every node is plain." width="100%"} Empties the selection, whether it holds nodes or edges (a graph never holds both). The nodes and edges themselves, and their attributes, are untouched; only the selection state is reset. `select_*` methods add to the existing selection by default, so calling `clear_selection()` before building a new selection is the usual way to make sure nothing left over from an earlier step leaks into the next `*_ws` operation (passing `set_op="replace"` to the `select_*` method does the same). It is also safe to call when nothing is selected. To remove only some nodes or edges from the selection, use `deselect_nodes()` or `deselect_edges()`. The graph is modified in place and returned for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The same graph (modified in place) for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The hub of this star is selected by degree and then the selection is cleared, so no nodes remain selected: ::: {#4e3ba41f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(5) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3) .clear_selection() ) graph.count_selected_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0 ``` ::: ::: Without clearing, selections accumulate. Here the second selection rule adds to the first (the hub plus the last two spokes), while clearing between the two calls leaves only the result of the second: ::: {#6548fe62 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(5) graph.select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=3).select_last_nodes_created(2) accumulated = graph.count_selected_nodes() graph.clear_selection().select_last_nodes_created(2) fresh = graph.count_selected_nodes() (accumulated, fresh) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 2) ``` ::: ::: An edge selection is cleared the same way. Here all four spoke edges are selected, which also drops the node selection, and then cleared: ::: {#d3b5d1b4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} hub = graph.get_node_creation_order()[0] graph.select_edges_by_node([hub]).clear_selection() graph.count_selected_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0 ``` ::: :::
